$description: #271 harvest lane B — PROPOSED `when` predicates for record-list + chart-panel + headline-metric + status-surface. s253-D1 shape (gate half + prose half). NOTHING ENACTED. No meta, schema, roles.json, rules index, runbook or gate was touched.
$shape: s253-D1: gate half = machine-checkable clause; prose half = beats/yields sentence naming the sibling and quoting its roles.json when.

$confidence_scale.canon: a predicate already adopted in our own repo — the work is a copy, not an invention
$confidence_scale.consensus-external: 3+ public systems state the same KIND of criterion
$confidence_scale.single-external: one system states it, or the systems conflict on the cut
$confidence_scale.none: no source found; the predicate is proposed from our own meta prose or is a declared guess

$note: 26 of these 45 already carry a `when` in roles.json or on the meta. For those the proposal is a COPY plus whatever external corroboration or contest the harvest turned up — the criterion itself is not being re-litigated (BRIEF rule). s270-D1 (single-select cut-off 5) is cited where it bears, never re-opened.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND fields-per-record >= 3 AND the reading is COMPARISON ACROSS records on the same fields AND interaction = none
proposals.when_prose: the default of the record-list role (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly"); beats list-items (roles.json when: "≤ 3 fields per item, tappable") whenever the reader must compare the same field down a column; yields to data-grid (roles.json when: "sort / filter / select / edit-in-place is required") the moment any interaction is needed, and to chart-panel when the claim is a shape rather than a value (USWDS: "consider a bar graph, infographic, or other type of chart").
disagreements: Polaris reaches the SAME split from a different discriminator: "A data table is a form of data visualization" — analysis vs action, not field count. Our number-of-fields test and their purpose test disagree on the middle case: a 5-field list of orders that are all links.
USWDS adds a rule we do not carry: a table yields to a CHART when the relationship is complex. No rule in our repo crosses record-list into chart-panel.
proposals.daves_call: only the copy onto the meta (#270's call, unchanged). NEW: whether to adopt USWDS's table→chart escape hatch as a real antiPattern.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND fields-per-record >= 3 AND (sort OR filter OR row-selection OR edit-in-place) is required
proposals.when_prose: beats table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") exactly when an interaction is required — the 2026-06-22 rubric decision A our meta already quotes; yields to table whenever the screen only reads, because a grid carries an ARIA grid contract a read-only page should not pay for.
disagreements: Ant Design does NOT make the split at all — one Table component covers "To display a collection of structured data" AND "To sort, search, paginate, filter data". Ant is the only system consulted that would call our two-component decision unnecessary.
proposals.daves_call: only the copy onto the meta. Same as table.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND fields-per-record <= 3 AND each row is TAPPABLE AND no field is compared down a column
proposals.when_prose: beats table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") when the row is a thing to open rather than a row to compare — roles.json when: "≤ 3 fields per item, tappable"; yields to table when a fourth field appears, and to data-grid when rows must be selected in bulk.
disagreements: the number 3 is OURS ALONE (already noted #270). Polaris offers the strongest rival formulation — "If your use case is more about finding and taking action on objects" — which is a PURPOSE test with no field count, and would admit a 6-field order row.
proposals.daves_call: #270's open question stands (is "tappable" REQUIRED). NEW: whether Polaris's action-vs-analysis test replaces or supplements the field count.

proposals.when_gate: the unit is a SELF-CONTAINED summary that links out AND items <= 6 AND no field is compared across items AND the surface groups content, not layout
proposals.when_prose: beats list-items when each item needs an image, a heading and its own action rather than a row of fields, and beats table absolutely — USWDS is explicit that a card is not a table row substitute; yields to table (roles.json when: "default, read-mostly") the moment the reader compares the same field across items, and yields to layout-utilities when the border is decoration.
disagreements: THE COUNT. USWDS names 6 ("Consider limiting the number of items in each collection to six or fewer"); Carbon, Polaris and Ant name none. Our meta names none.
USWDS ALSO has a separate `collection` component for the compact metadata case that sits between our cards and list-items — a component we do not have.
proposals.daves_call: whether cards carries a MAXIMUM item count at all, and if so whether it is USWDS's 6. Also: is "not a table row substitute" a hard antiPattern here?

proposals.when_gate: the records are issued documents to open / download AND each row carries file-type + period + format + size AND a trailing download control exists AND no amount is shown
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "the records are issued documents to open / download"; beats list-items because the row carries a nested download control that list-items' whole-row tap would swallow (our AP0, the defect this component exists to prevent); yields to file-upload for files the user is sending (our own AP3).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — no system consulted has a document-row. This is a domain component; silence is expected, not a gap.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Copy the adopted predicate onto the meta.

proposals.when_gate: the records are a ledger AND a RUNNING BALANCE is present AND rows are NOT individually tappable AND day grouping + closing total exist
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "the records are a ledger with a running balance"; beats list-items because the question is "what was the balance after this?", a relation BETWEEN rows, and therefore a table (our own purpose); yields to list-items the instant the running balance is dropped or the row becomes tappable — our AP0 and AP1 say each of those turns it back into a list.
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — domain component.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Copy. (The meta is still marked PROPOSED #209, NOT GATED — that is a separate status question, not a when question.)

proposals.when_gate: the records are future recurring instructions AND each carries payee + amount + rhythm + next date + state AND exactly two actions (open, manage)
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "the records are future recurring instructions"; beats transaction-row (roles.json when: "ledger with a running balance") because nothing has happened yet and there is no balance to run; beats list-items because the manage control cannot be nested inside a whole-row button (our AP1).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — domain component. Our own AP0 (standing order ≠ direct debit) has no external analogue either.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Copy.

proposals.when_gate: records = 1 AND the record IS an account (label · masked number · balance) AND the reading is passive AND an optional type tag + RAG chip may be present
proposals.when_prose: the single-account readout; beats stat-card (roles.json when: "default — label · value · delta · period, no series") because the number is a BALANCE belonging to a named account rather than a metric with a delta; beats payment-card-visual (our AP1: "a payment-card visual with a balance is an Account-card wearing a card shape") whenever money is on the face; yields to account-selector (#270 proposal) once the card becomes a choice.
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — no system consulted has an account card. The account-card / payment-card-visual boundary is stated only in payment-card-visual's antiPattern, not on account-card itself.
proposals.daves_call: whether the balance-on-the-face test is the fence between account-card and payment-card-visual, and whether it should be written on BOTH metas rather than one.

proposals.when_gate: records >= 2 AND time IS the structure AND every record has ALREADY HAPPENED AND entries are not buttons AND order is newest-first with date headings
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "time is the structure, records have happened"; beats list-items when the date rail is the reading rather than a sort order; yields to list-items inside a date group the moment entries must open (our AP1), and never borrows Progress-tracker's aria-current because there is no current step (our AP0).
disagreements: none — Ant reaches the same line ("When a series of information needs to be ordered by time"). Ant does NOT carry our past-tense-only restriction, which is the sharper half of our rule.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Copy. Worth noting our "records have happened" is stricter than every external analogue.

proposals.when_gate: records NEST AND depth >= 2 AND one node selectable at a time AND depth carried by aria-level AND the tree is NOT the product's primary navigation
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "records nest"; beats list-items and accordion when the containment relation itself is the information (our purpose: "where a flat list would lose the containment relation"); yields to list-items when there is only one level of nesting (Carbon states this as a when-not-to-use) and to sidebar-nav when it would be the primary nav (Carbon again).
disagreements: Carbon fences the tree twice (one level → use a list; never as primary nav). Ant fences it not at all: "Almost anything can be represented in a tree structure." Our roles.json "records nest" is closer to Ant than to Carbon.
Our meta sets a depth FLOOR of level 5 for the indent ladder; nobody outside names a depth limit.
proposals.daves_call: whether to import Carbon's two exclusions (single-level → list-items; never primary navigation) as antiPatterns.

proposals.when_gate: sections >= 2 AND the reader needs only SOME sections AND no section is required reading for everyone AND multiple sections may be open at once
proposals.when_prose: beats a plain scrolling page only when the evidence says readers want a few sections, not all of them — four systems say so independently; yields to an Expand link when there is a single disclosure (our own AP0, per HSBC guidance, and GOV.UK names a component for it: "Use the details component instead of tabs or an accordion"); yields to tabs (slice C) when the sections are alternative views rather than optional depth.
disagreements: MULTI-OPEN. NN/g: "make sure to give people the capability to open multiple sections at a time". Ant defines the word the other way: an Accordion is the Collapse variant that allows ONLY ONE panel open. Our meta is silent on which we are.
No system gives a section-count floor or ceiling. Our proposed ">= 2" comes from our own single-accordion antiPattern, not from a source.
proposals.daves_call: one word: is our Accordion multi-open (NN/g) or single-open (Ant's definition)? Everything else here is unanimous.

proposals.when_gate: NONE PROPOSED — the lane recommends this component carry a when that says "do not, unless the content is genuinely peer-level and non-essential"
proposals.when_prose: every system consulted that speaks warns against it; the honest predicate is a negative one — a carousel is legitimate only where the items are peers, none is essential, and the same content is reachable elsewhere (NN/g: "some people will only see the first frame or none at all"); yields to a static hero (slice C) or a stacked list in every other case.
sources: OUR meta carousel.purpose (PROPOSED #210, not registered, not ruled)
disagreements: Ant is the ONLY system consulted that recommends a carousel without a warning ("When there is a group of content on the same level"). NN/g, and by implication GOV.UK and USWDS which ship no carousel at all, are against.
GOV.UK, USWDS, Carbon and Polaris have NO carousel component. That is four systems' worth of structural silence.
proposals.daves_call: whether Carousel stays in the library at all. If it does, whether its `when` is written as a permission or as a warning.

proposals.when_gate: items > N (N unruled) AND the split is by VOLUME ONLY, not by meaning AND the journey is NOT linear AND infinite scroll is not used instead
proposals.when_prose: beats showing everything once the list is long enough to cost load time or scroll (Carbon: "When there is too much data to display on one page"); yields to stepper/progress-tracker for a linear journey — GOV.UK and Carbon both forbid pagination there in the same words; yields to nothing for infinite scroll, which GOV.UK and NN/g both advise against.
sources: USWDS pagination (silent on the criterion — measured)
disagreements: THE NUMBER. Polaris is the ONLY system that names one: "Paginate when the current list contains more than 50 items." Carbon, GOV.UK, Ant give no number at all. USWDS's page carries no when-to-use section whatsoever.
So this is the record-list twin of #270's radio→dropdown finding: the KIND is unanimous, the CUT exists in exactly one system.
proposals.daves_call: pick 50 (Polaris), pick our own number, or rule that we carry no number and use "more than one screen of rows" instead. Same decision shape as s270-D1.

proposals.when_gate: a record-list or chart-panel is present AND >= 2 of {search, filter, date-range, view-switch, result-count, applied-filter chips, export} are needed AND every control is an existing gated atom
proposals.when_prose: the bar that DRIVES a list; beats scattering the same controls above a table because it fixes the composition order and the applied-filter chip row; composes only — it re-draws no atom (our AP0, the #202 defect), consumes Segmented-control not View-options for the view switch (our AP1), and hands "Custom range…" to date-range-picker rather than copying its calendar (our AP2).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — no system consulted names a filter toolbar as a component. Carbon's data-table page describes the same controls as part of the table; Polaris folds them into IndexTable. Two systems treat this as a table FEATURE, not a component.
That is a finding worth Dave's eye: our decision to make the bar a separate composition has no external precedent either way.
proposals.daves_call: confirm the ">= 2 controls" floor, or rule that the bar is legal with one.

proposals.when_gate: NEVER — superseded 2026-07-24; the view switch is Segmented-control
proposals.when_prose: carries no selection criterion because it is not a choice any composer should make: filter-toolbar-bar's AP1 already says "Consuming View-options instead of Segmented-control for the view switch — View-options was superseded"; the honest `when` here is a redirect, not a predicate.
disagreements: none. This is a housekeeping finding, not a harvest result: a superseded component is sitting in the library with a purpose statement that reads like a live recommendation.
proposals.daves_call: whether a superseded component gets a `when` that says "do not", or gets removed from the library. Either way it should not read as available.

proposals.when_gate: series >= 2 AND label = text AND the charts keyed are MORE THAN ONE (small multiples or a comparison row) AND colour is not the only channel
proposals.when_prose: our meta already states it: "a key is needed only where more than one series is drawn; a single-series chart names its series in the title"; placed on its own ONLY for small multiples — a lone chart carries its legend inside its own figure; never colour-only (our AP3, and NN/g: "color should not be used to communicate information about quantitative").
disagreements: A CEILING NOBODY IN OUR REPO CARRIES. Spectrum: "The ideal usage for these is when there are 8 or fewer categories" being colour-coded. Our legend has no maximum series count; our isoluminant categorical set's size is a separate token question.
proposals.daves_call: whether to adopt a series/category ceiling on the legend (Spectrum's 8, or our own), and whether that ceiling is the legend's rule or the palette's.

proposals.when_gate: answers = comparison AND axis.x = categorical AND baseline = 0 (dv-bar-009); stacked variant when composition across categories
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "comparison; stacked variant when composition across categories"; beats chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") when x is categorical rather than a time continuum, and beats chart-pie (roles.json: "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts") when the parts do not sum to a whole — NN/g put it plainly: "Bar charts are a reliable means of representing quantitative data".
disagreements: ORIENTATION. FT gives a rule we carry nowhere: horizontal bar is "Good when the data are not time series and labels have long category names". Our meta treats vertical/horizontal as a variant with no selection criterion — and our AP1 forbids negatives on the horizontal form, which is an unrelated constraint.

GROUPED SERIES CEILING. FT: "Can become tricky to read with more than 2 series". Our meta names no series ceiling for grouped bars, yet Chart-butterfly REQUIRES exactly 2. The two rules are adjacent and unreconciled.
STACKED CATEGORY CEILING. Datawrapper: "If you have more than approximately 10 categories" switch to horizontal. We carry no such number.
proposals.daves_call: three numbers, all currently absent: the horizontal/vertical rule, the grouped-series ceiling, and the stacked-category ceiling.

proposals.when_gate: answers = change-over-time AND series 1–5 on ONE continuous time axis AND axes = present AND span.cols >= 6
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "change-over-time" — the role's default at this intent; yields to chart-combo (roles.json: "two measures in different units over one axis") when units differ, to Chart-candlestick when all four OHLC points are the claim, and to chart-sparkline when the panel cannot carry axes; Datawrapper states the gate in our own words: "Use line charts only if you want to show how values develop over time."
disagreements: FEW POINTS. Datawrapper: with only a few values at the same intervals, "consider a column chart instead". FT agrees from the other side: columns over time are "usually best with only one series of data at a time". We have no lower bound on line-chart point count and no upper bound on columns-over-time series.

BASELINE. Datawrapper: "Line charts have the big advantage that they don’t need to start from zero." Our dv-bar-009 forces bars to zero but says nothing about line; the asymmetry is correct but undocumented as a CHOICE criterion.
proposals.daves_call: whether a point-count floor pushes change-over-time to chart-bar, and if so what it is.

proposals.when_gate: answers = change-over-time AND series = 2 AND units = DIFFERENT AND both read against ONE shared x (dv-line-006)
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "two measures in different units over one axis"; beats chart-line on the different-units test and on nothing else; yields to chart-line (multi-series) or chart-bar (grouped) for a same-unit pair, which our own antiPattern forbids drawing here.
disagreements: THE INTENT WORD. The FT files this shape under CORRELATION first ("showing the relationship between an amount (columns) and a rate (line)") and under Change v Time second. Our answers axis says change-over-time only. If a composer's claim is the relationship, our gate sends them to Chart-scatter, which cannot draw it.
proposals.daves_call: whether chart-combo answers change-over-time only, or change-over-time AND relationship. This is an answers-axis change, not a meta edit.

proposals.when_gate: answers = composition AND parts sum to a whole AND parts <= 6 AND total = printed as a centre figure
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "composition, a centre total is meaningful"; beats chart-pie whenever the total is worth printing and on nothing else (our own meta); yields to chart-stacked-area (roles.json: "composition over time") when the split MOVES; the FT reaches our exact discriminator: "the centre can be a good way of making space to include more information".
disagreements: NN/g RANKS DONUT BELOW PIE — "made even less effective by the whitespace in the middle", "their even less helpful cousin". roles.json ranks donut ABOVE pie (donut is the default composition provider at weight 80; pie is 48). One system inverts our own ordering.
SLICE CEILING. Our `when` says the parts sum to a whole with no count; our antiPattern says 6; roles.json's PIE entry says 5. Three numbers for the same family, none of them the same.
proposals.daves_call: the slice ceiling for the pie/donut family (5, 6, or two different numbers on purpose), and whether NN/g's ranking changes anything.

proposals.when_gate: answers = composition AND parts >= 3 AND parts <= 5 AND total = not printed
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts"; yields to chart-donut whenever a centre total is wanted, which is the only thing separating the two; yields to chart-bar when the reader must compare share sizes rather than see one dominant share — Datawrapper: "Pie charts are not the best choice if you want readers to compare".
disagreements: THE CEILING AGREES FOR ONCE: Datawrapper's "If you have more than five shares, consider a stacked column" matches roles.json's ≤ 5 exactly. Our own antiPattern says 6. The disagreement is INTERNAL, not external.
THE FLOOR IS NEW. Datawrapper: "Pie charts might be unnecessary if you only want to show two values" — a lower bound (>= 3) nobody in our repo carries.
THE COMPONENT ITSELF. NN/g: "visualizations like pie charts and tree maps are generally not recommended" for a dashboard. GOV.UK, USWDS and Carbon ship no pie guidance at all in what we could reach.
proposals.daves_call: add the lower bound (>= 3 parts)? And fix the 5-vs-6 internal clash — the same word cannot be both.

proposals.when_gate: answers = change-over-time AND series = 1 AND axes = absent AND span.cols <= 4
proposals.when_prose: our meta's own when; yields to chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") whenever the panel can carry axes, and is normally a complement of headline-metric rather than a chart-panel in its own right (ROLES-REVIEW §03); a standalone spark without its table is forbidden (dv-005) because the shape alone is not data.
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — not one system consulted names a sparkline. It is also absent from roles.json's chart-panel provider list, so it has a meta `when` and no role seat.
The FT Visual Vocabulary has no sparkline row either.
proposals.daves_call: whether chart-sparkline belongs in chart-panel's provider list, in headline-metric's, or in neither (a slot, not a provider).

proposals.when_gate: answers spans change-over-time AND composition AND cumulative bands share ONE total across the time axis AND dates >= ~10
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "composition over time"; beats chart-donut and chart-pie when the split MOVES rather than being a snapshot; yields to chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") when the total is not meaningful — Datawrapper says it in our words: "Area charts work best if the total is as important as its shares."
disagreements: A DATE FLOOR WE DO NOT CARRY. Datawrapper: "If you have less than ten or so dates, consider a stacked column". Our when has no date count, so a 4-quarter split is legal as a stacked area here and would be a stacked column at Datawrapper.
FT is markedly more hostile than we are: "seeing change in components can be very difficult", filed under "Use with care".
proposals.daves_call: adopt a date floor (~10) for stacked area, or rule that we carry none.

proposals.when_gate: answers = distribution AND categories >= 2 AND each category carries a five-number summary AND span.cols <= 8
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "distribution per category"; beats Chart-histogram (roles.json: "distribution, one variable") whenever the spread must be read PER CATEGORY; yields to it when variables = 1 and the bin shape is the claim.
disagreements: none — FT states the same job ("Summarise multiple distributions by showing the median (centre) and range of the data"). FT adds violin as the escalation for complex distributions; we have no violin.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Free.

proposals.when_gate: answers = comparison AND the reading is one measure against a TARGET plus qualitative bands AND span.cols 4–6
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta"; beats stat-card and kpi-tile when the BENCHMARK is the point; and it is the ONLY provider allowed to draw a target — meter's AP1 and runway-bar's AP1 both say "a bar with a target IS a Chart-bullet and should be one".
disagreements: MEASURED EXTERNAL SILENCE, AND IT IS LOUD. The FT Visual Vocabulary lists Bullet as a chart type with an EMPTY description field — the only such row in the file. No other system consulted has one. Our two most-fenced components (meter, runway-bar) both redirect to a component with zero external corroboration.
proposals.daves_call: none on the criterion — but note that the whole target-bar fence in this role rests on one unsourced component.

proposals.when_gate: answers = comparison AND series = 2 mirrored outward from a shared centre gutter AND categories >= 6
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "exactly two series mirrored, categories ≥ 6"; beats grouped chart-bar when the two series must read as OPPOSED directions rather than adjacent columns; yields to Chart-butterfly-v when the category axis is ordered left-to-right and span.cols >= 8.
disagreements: THE INTENT WORD AGAIN. The FT files the back-to-back form under DISTRIBUTION — "effectively, back to back histograms" — not comparison. Our answers axis says comparison. A composer whose claim is an age/sex distribution is gated away from the one chart that draws it.
FT also independently supplies the 2-series ceiling from the bar side ("tricky to read with more than 2 series"), which corroborates our exactly-2 requirement.
proposals.daves_call: whether Chart-butterfly answers comparison only, or comparison AND distribution.

proposals.when_gate: answers = comparison AND series = 2 mirrored above/below ONE horizontal baseline AND the category axis is ORDERED left-to-right AND span.cols >= 8
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "as above, wide panel"; yields to Chart-butterfly-h whenever the categories are unordered or the panel is narrower than 8 cols; both yield to chart-bar (grouped) when the pair is not genuinely opposed.
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE on the h-vs-v split. No system consulted distinguishes them; the ordered-axis + 8-col test is ours alone.
Inherits the same distribution-vs-comparison clash as the h form.
proposals.daves_call: same single call as butterfly-h; the h/v split itself needs no ruling.

proposals.when_gate: answers = change-over-time AND shape = periods × OHLC (open · high · low · close per session)
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "OHLC per period"; beats chart-line (roles.json: "change-over-time") only when all four price points per period are the claim; yields to chart-line whenever one measure's path is enough.
disagreements: none — FT states the same content ("show opening/closing and hi/low points of each day"). FT marks its stock-price entry as NOT available in their toolkit; ours is built.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Free.

proposals.when_gate: answers = distribution AND variables = 1 AND bins = contiguous (no inter-bar gap) AND baseline = 0
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "distribution, one variable"; beats Chart-boxplot (roles.json: "distribution per category") when the frequency shape of ONE variable is the claim; yields to Chart-boxplot when categories >= 2; the no-gap rule is not cosmetic — the FT gives the same reason: "keep the gaps between columns small to highlight the 'shape' of the data".
disagreements: none. This is the cleanest chart in the slice — our gate, our antiPattern and the FT's description all say the same thing.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Free.

proposals.when_gate: answers = relationship AND both axes carry quantitative measures
proposals.when_prose: the ONLY provider of relationship in the role, so it beats every sibling on the answers gate alone; yields to chart-combo when the two measures share one x axis in different units instead of being plotted against each other — NN/g and the FT both state the job in the same terms.
disagreements: Being the sole provider is a fragility, not an agreement: the FT lists five more Correlation types (bubble, connected scatter, XY heatmap, line-column, scatter-line-timeline). Four of the five we cannot draw, and one of them (line-column) IS our chart-combo filed under a different intent.
proposals.daves_call: nothing on the criterion. The gap list is a finding for the roadmap.

proposals.when_gate: shape = one-measure × value-and-delta AND series = none AND delta != none
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "default — label · value · delta · period, no series"; beats kpi-tile (roles.json: "a series exists to show") exactly when no series exists — s247-D3 / DP-08: no series ⇒ not a KPI tile; yields to Chart-bullet when a target is the point and to runway-bar when the reading is money against what is already scheduled.
disagreements: THE DELTA REQUIREMENT IS OURS ALONE. Ant's Statistic — the only external analogue found in this whole role — requires nothing but a number: "When want to highlight some data." Our gate says delta != none, which would make a bare balance illegal as a Stat card.
No system consulted has a four-provider headline-metric role. This role's internal fences are entirely ours.
proposals.daves_call: is a delta REQUIRED for a Stat card? If it is, name the component that shows a number with no delta and no series (today: nothing in this role).

proposals.when_gate: shape = one-measure × value-delta-and-series AND series != none
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "a series exists to show (s247-D3 / DP-08: no series ⇒ not a KPI tile)"; beats stat-card whenever a series exists; yields to Chart-bullet (roles.json: "a target or performance band is the point, not the delta") when target != none, and to runway-bar when the reading is committed-vs-balance.
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — no system consulted splits a metric tile by whether it carries a series.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Copy.

proposals.when_gate: shape = rows × name-value-pairs AND rows >= 2 AND span.cols >= 6 AND the reading is confirmation, not comparison
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "n × count as a key/value list, 6–12 cols"; beats status-indicator (roles.json: "one state, one dot + label, 2–4 cols") whenever more than one row must be read at once; yields to meter when the threshold is a cap being spent against; and it is a description list, not a table (our AP0).
disagreements: GOV.UK's summary-list (cited in #270) fences it from the other side: "Do not use it for tabular data or a simple list of information or tasks". Ant's Descriptions is the same shape with no fence at all ("Commonly displayed on the details page").
roles.json places summary in STATUS-SURFACE ("n × count"); our meta describes a payment-review receipt. Those are two different components wearing one name.
proposals.daves_call: which summary is it — the count board (roles.json) or the review receipt (the meta)? They need different whens, possibly different components.

proposals.when_gate: a value sits on a track between a min and a max AND (variant = allowance ⇒ full means BLOCKED) AND no target marker AND no qualitative bands
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "the threshold is a cap being spent against (limits-meter reading)"; one component covers progress and allowance as SEMANTIC VARIANTS — s210-D1, Dave verbatim: "keep as one meter"; yields to Chart-bullet the moment a target marker or qualitative band appears (our AP1); the fill is never painted red at the ceiling (our AP0).
disagreements: THE ROLL-UP ITSELF. Spectrum keeps Meter and ProgressBar as SEPARATE components with a real, testable discriminator: "Their progress is determined by user actions, rather than system actions." Carbon likewise ships progress-bar with a determinate/indeterminate split and no meter at all. Our s210-D1 merged them; Spectrum's test would un-merge them.
Nobody outside distinguishes an ALLOWANCE meter (full = blocked) from a PROGRESS meter (full = done). That semantic — the whole point of our limits-meter variant — is ours alone.
proposals.daves_call: s210-D1 is ruled and this lane does not re-open it. The question is narrower: does Spectrum's user-action-vs-system-action test become the named discriminator BETWEEN our variants, since we have nothing else separating them?

proposals.when_gate: INHERITS meter's gate, variant = allowance: the value is a cap being spent against AND full = BLOCKED, not done
proposals.when_prose: a thin category alias of meter.meta.json (s210-D5); carries no independent when because writing spec into the alias is an explicit antiPattern on the parent — the reading is "how much of my limit is left", which is what roles.json already names.
disagreements: none — but note that if a `when` is ever WRITTEN onto this alias it breaches s210-D5. Any gate that requires a `when` on every meta will force that breach. Flagged as a mechanism problem, not a content one.
proposals.daves_call: whether alias metas are EXEMPT from a future when-completeness gate. This is a gate-design call, and it bites before the whens land.

proposals.when_gate: answers = one-number AND shape = one-measure × committed-vs-balance-split AND verdict != none AND a DATE is part of the takeaway
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "the number is 'money vs what is already scheduled'"; beats stat-card and kpi-tile when the takeaway is a VERDICT WITH A DATE rather than a value with a delta; yields to Chart-bullet if a target marker is added (our AP1) — this component has no target, it has a horizon; the bar is never coloured by verdict (our AP0).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — domain component. The nearest thing found is FT's spine chart, "Splits a single value into 2 contrasting components", which is the geometry but not the verdict.
proposals.daves_call: nothing. Copy.

proposals.when_gate: a currency value is rendered ANYWHERE — this is a primitive, not a choice: symbol/code with no space (copy-025), tabular lining figures, U+2212 for negatives, redactable
proposals.when_prose: carries no selection criterion because there is no sibling to beat: every component that prints money composes it verbatim (stat-card does, by name); it is monochrome by design and directional gain/loss colour belongs to the host, not to the primitive.
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE on the component; Polaris independently reaches our alignment rule from the table side.

A primitive with no sibling has no when. Worth deciding whether the schema should say `when: null, reason: primitive` rather than leaving the field empty — the same shape roles.json used for undiscriminated providers.
proposals.daves_call: whether primitives get an explicit null-with-reason or stay blank.

proposals.when_gate: tiles >= 2 of {stat-card, kpi-tile} AND a section heading is present AND the row auto-fills AND no new molecule is drawn
proposals.when_prose: the labelled row of metric tiles; beats hand-rolling the dashboard KPI section (which Template-dashboard already does) because it fixes the heading + auto-fill grid once; composes Layout-utilities, Stat-card, Kpi-tile and Cards' arrow-link ONLY — a new molecule here is an explicit do-not-rule (our AP1).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — lock-ups are our own layer; no system consulted names one.
The tile floor (>= 2) is proposed from the word "row", not from a source.
proposals.daves_call: confirm the >= 2 tile floor, or rule that a one-tile band is legal.

proposals.when_gate: the content is a COUNT (or a bare dot) AND it is attached to another element AND it is passive AND it is not the only carrier of critical information
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "inline, attached to another element, count only"; beats status-indicator (roles.json: "one state, one dot + label, 2–4 cols") because a badge carries a number attached to a host, not a state with a word; beats tags because a tag names a property and a badge counts one; never carries information that must not be missed (our AP0) — that is Alert (slice A).
disagreements: THE WORD IS OVERLOADED ACROSS SYSTEMS AND THIS IS THE REAL FINDING. Ant's Badge = our Badge ("typically displaying unread messages count"). Spectrum's Badge = our Tags/Status-indicator ("a small amount of color-categorized metadata"). Polaris's Badge = our Status-indicator ("Use a single word to describe the tone of an object"). USWDS folds all three jobs into one `tag`.
So the count-only fence is unanimous only among the systems that use the word our way — one of four.
proposals.daves_call: nothing on our criterion (it is canon and it is clean). But the naming collision is worth knowing before any external prose is quoted into a Badge spec.

proposals.when_gate: the content is a KEYWORD describing the item's property or category (not a state, not a count) AND >= 0 may apply at once
proposals.when_prose: beats badge (roles.json: "inline, attached to another element, count only") because a tag names a property rather than counting one; beats status-indicator (roles.json: "one state, one dot + label") because a state is a single RAG-coded fact and a keyword set is not; our static/interactive split has no external support and two systems forbid the interactive form outright.
disagreements: THE INTERACTIVE TAG. Our meta ships a "Tag link". GOV.UK: "Do not use tags to create links, buttons or other interactive elements". Carbon: "Do not use tags as links that direct you to an entirely different page". USWDS: "Users frequently confuse tags as buttons." Three systems against one of our own variants.

WHAT A TAG IS. Carbon and Ant say KEYWORD ("tag by dimension or property"). GOV.UK says STATUS ("Use the Tag component to show users the status of something") — GOV.UK's Tag is our Status-indicator. The systems do not agree on the component, so they cannot agree on its when.
proposals.daves_call: does our Tag link survive three systems saying don't? And is our Tag a keyword (Carbon/Ant) or a status (GOV.UK)? The second answer decides whether tags and status-indicator overlap.

proposals.when_gate: exactly ONE state is read AND it is rendered as dot + WORD AND span.cols <= 4 AND the dot is never the only carrier
proposals.when_prose: roles.json when: "one state, one dot + label, 2–4 cols" — the default of the role; beats summary (roles.json: "n × count as a key/value list, 6–12 cols") whenever exactly one state is read; yields to badge when the dot is attached to another element rather than standing alone; the label is mandatory (our AP0, and the dot measures 1.98:1 standalone per #204).
disagreements: THE COPY RULES ARE EXTERNAL AND WE HAVE NONE. Polaris: "Use a single word to describe the tone of an object" and "Always describe the tone in the past tense." GOV.UK: "Sometimes a single status is enough" — i.e. absence of a chip is itself a state. Our meta carries no copy rule for the label at all.
Spectrum caps colour-coded categories at 8; our RAG set is 4 + disabled, so we are inside it — but the ceiling is not written down anywhere in our repo.
proposals.daves_call: adopt the past-tense single-word copy rule (Polaris), and rule whether an ABSENT chip may mean a state (GOV.UK's move).

proposals.when_gate: the subject is a PERSON or an ENTITY AND the representation is compact and circular AND it is never the sole accessible label for a control
proposals.when_prose: beats an icon when the identity of the individual matters; yields to a thumbnail for an object rather than a person or business (Polaris names a component for that; we have none); yields to avatar-group once the unit of meaning is the set rather than the individual (our own avatar-group purpose).
sources: Ant avatar (no when-to-use section — measured silence)
disagreements: Polaris supplies the only real fence found: person/business vs object. We have no thumbnail component, so that fence currently has nowhere to point.
Ant's avatar page carries NO when-to-use section at all. Spectrum's Avatar docs carry no guidance prose. Measured silence in two systems.
proposals.daves_call: whether "person or entity" is the fence, and what an object-thumbnail should be in our library (Cards' image slot? Image-block, slice C?).

proposals.when_gate: people >= 2 AND the unit of meaning is the GROUP AND an overflow counter appears past the display cap AND no 32px disc is interactive
proposals.when_prose: our meta's own claim: the unit of meaning is the GROUP ("five people are on this approval"), not the individuals; beats a row of Avatars because the count is the reading and the stack must not be announced disc-by-disc (our AP1); the '+3' is never the only place the count exists (our AP2).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE by fetch failure, not by absence — Atlassian ships an Avatar Group with published guidance we could not extract (see refused). Treat this row's silence as UNMEASURED.
The display cap has no number in our meta and none was found.
proposals.daves_call: the display cap number, if we want one. Otherwise nothing.

proposals.when_gate: the subject is a PHYSICAL payment instrument AND the reading is 'which card is this and can I use it' AND NO balance is shown AND the PAN is masked by default
proposals.when_prose: beats account-card exactly when there is no balance — our own AP1 draws the line: "a payment-card visual with a balance is an Account-card wearing a card shape"; carries no network mark, issuer logotype or EMV chip artwork (our AP0, licensed outside this system).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — domain component, expected.
proposals.daves_call: nothing beyond the account-card fence question already raised there.

proposals.when_gate: a string must cross to a second device AND the same content is repeated as text AND the matrix is a REAL encoding AND the quiet zone is inside the artwork AND the box scales with payload length
proposals.when_prose: carries no sibling to beat — its `when` is a set of conditions on legitimacy, not a choice: a plausible-texture matrix is worse than no QR code (our AP0), a cropped quiet zone breaks the symbol (our AP1), and a fixed outer box shrinks modules below scannability as payloads grow (our AP2).
disagreements: EXTERNAL SILENCE — no design system consulted ships a QR component with usage guidance.
Like amount-display, this is a component whose `when` is a validity contract rather than a discriminator. The schema shape assumes a sibling exists.
proposals.daves_call: whether the schema admits a `when` with no sibling (validity conditions), or those belong entirely in antiPatterns.
